expectations.text: OUTPUT_DIR/plan.md exists and contains, in order, sections for: headline, approach summary, out of scope, plan steps, assumptions, test plan, risks and mitigations, open questions (names may vary slightly).
expectations.evidence: plan.md exists (26538 bytes). H2 headings by line: Headline (3), Approach summary (13), Out of scope (34), Plan (45), Assumptions validated (116), Test plan (296), Risks and mitigations (349), Open questions (368). All eight present and in order. check_run.py reported sections_in_order=false only because its 'plan' keyword matched the H1 title '# Plan: overdue tickets...' at index 0; the H2 order is correct.

expectations.text: The headline is one to three sentences and states what is being built and the chosen approach; the approach summary is prose of three to ten sentences, not bullets.
expectations.evidence: Headline has four sentences: 'Compute "overdue" on the fly ... sorted by due time.' / 'No new event, no new ticket state, no new file: ... already holds.' / 'One decision blocks implementation: ... every spec edit.' / 'The plan proceeds on the assumption that a closed ticket is never overdue.' Content is right (what and approach in sentence 1) but the count exceeds three. Approach summary is two prose paragraphs, eight sentences, no bullets, which satisfies its half.

expectations.text: The plan states a falsifier for the hypothesis: an observation that would prove the chosen shape wrong, separate from the individual assumptions.
expectations.evidence: Section 'Hypothesis and falsifier (recorded)' (lines 101-114): 'What would have proved the shape wrong: (a) a requirement to persist overdue (a new event kind) ... (b) a requirement that overdue be a state in TKT-001 ... (c) the service having no access to a clock ...' followed by why none held. Separate from the 'Assumptions validated' section.

expectations.text: Project conventions are cited with file:line from AGENTS.md or docs/guidelines.md: the test framework is unittest run by `make test`, lint is `make lint`, and no package manager or test runner from outside the repo (pytest, poetry, npm) is assumed.
expectations.evidence: '[AGENTS.md:19-25, architecture.md:73-82] Convention: Python 3.11+, argparse, unittest via make test, compileall via make lint' and '[Makefile:2-5, README.md:7, guidelines.md:12-13] make test runs python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -q; make lint runs compileall'. Verified: AGENTS.md:22-23 are the Tests/Lint rows, guidelines.md:12-13 is 'Run both before you push', Makefile:2-5 matches. check_run foreign_tools=[]; grep for pytest/poetry/npm in plan.md finds nothing.

Line numbers verified against the fixture (TKT-005 at tickets.md:36, TKT-013 at :83, CLI-001 at cli.md:12, CLI-006 at cli.md:39).

expectations.text: The plan respects INV-001 and INV-002: overdue status is derived from the ticket's due time at read time and is never written to the event log as an edit or a new event, or if an event is proposed, the plan flags it as a spec change needing user approval.
expectations.evidence: Out of scope: 'Recording overdue in the log, or any new event kind (LOG-002 unchanged)'. Spec table: 'INV-001 ... Holds | No cache or file; computed per command' and 'INV-002 ... Holds | Store untouched'. Step 3 computes is_overdue(now) at call time; prototype confirmed 'the six-line log stayed six lines after both commands'. No event is proposed.

expectations.text: The plan reuses the existing due_at value on Ticket (or ticketdesk.sla.due_at) instead of recomputing SLA hours in the CLI or a new module.
expectations.evidence: Step 3: 'def is_overdue(self, now): return self.state != "closed" and now > self.due_at'. Out of scope: 'Any change to ticketdesk/store.py, ticketdesk/sla.py'. Assumption: 'due_at is set on every replayed ticket. Verified: tickets.py:36 sets t.due_at = due_at(ev["at"], ev["priority"])' which matches the fixture source.

expectations.text: The plan names where `now` comes from for the overdue comparison (an injectable clock or time source consistent with EventStore.clock) and validates that assumption against the code.
expectations.evidence: Step 3: 'TicketService ... add now() returning self.store.clock()'. Assumptions: 'Service reaches the clock. Verified: EventStore.__init__ stores clock at store.py:14-16; TicketService keeps self.store at tickets.py:28. Prototype: svc.overdue() returned results driven by the fake clock.' Both citations match the fixture. It also found the fake Clock's tick-per-call side effect (tests/test_tickets.py:12-14) and planned around it.

expectations.text: Every load-bearing assumption in the assumptions section carries evidence: a file:line citation, a quoted doc passage, or a command output.
expectations.evidence: All 11 bullets in 'Assumptions validated' carry evidence, e.g. 'Verified: tickets.py:36 ...; sla.py:6-9 returns a float', 'Confirmed by experiment: after one svc.overdue() call clock.now advanced by exactly 1 (tests/test_tickets.py:12-14)', 'Confirmed: 7 existing plus 3 prototype tests, all green; make lint clean'. check_run counts 95 file:line citations in the plan; spot-checked ~20 and all resolve to the cited content.

expectations.text: The test plan names unittest test files under tests/ and at least these cases: a ticket exactly at its due time, a closed ticket past due (expected not overdue, or flagged as an open question), and the ordering of the overdue list.
expectations.evidence: Test plan names tests/test_tickets.py (new cases in TicketTests) and tests/test_cli.py (new, subprocess). Cases: 'test_not_overdue_before_or_at_due_time_TKT014: ... call returns exactly due_at; overdue() is empty (boundary)', 'test_closed_ticket_never_overdue_TKT014: create P1, close it, move the clock a week ahead; overdue() is empty', 'test_overdue_sorted_by_due_then_id_TKT015: create P3, P1, P2 ...; overdue() is [P1, P2, P3]' plus CLI 'test_overdue_lists_oldest_due_first_CLI010'.

Confirmed by prototype.') and ends 'Verdict: Confirmed with gaps. Gaps: (a) the spec edits in steps 1-2 await sign-off; (b) the overdue definition ... is an assumption until confirmed.'

expectations.text: Open questions are listed explicitly (for example whether closed tickets count as overdue, the exit code when nothing is overdue) and none is silently answered in the plan steps without being named as an assumption.
expectations.evidence: Eight open questions, each with 'Assumed ...': closed tickets (Q1, assumed no), due exactly now (Q2, strict >), marker placement (Q3), lateness display (Q4), spec edits (Q5), first CLI test (Q6), tie-break (Q7), commit shape (Q8). Empty-overdue exit code is not an open question but is not silently decided either: the plan derives exit 0 from existing CLI-006/CLI-008 ('CLI-008 success exit ... Holds | Prototype: exit 0, empty stderr') and writes it into the proposed CLI-010 text.

prose-lint.py reports '91 findings in 1 file', exit 1: roughly 70 semicolon findings, 10 long-sentence (up to 64 words at line 108), 6 long-lead (headline lead 31 words at line 5, approach lead 32 words at line 23). check_run lint_findings=91.

expectations.text: Skim test: the first sentence of each paragraph in the headline and approach summary carries a claim a newcomer understands; no step numbers, shorthand, or teaser leads.
expectations.evidence: Headline lead: 'Compute "overdue" on the fly in the service layer from the store's clock, mark overdue lines in ticketdesk list with a trailing OVERDUE, and add ticketdesk overdue, which prints only overdue tickets sorted by due time.' Approach para 1: 'A ticket is overdue when it is not closed and the current time is later than its due time.' Para 2: 'The approach stands on two assumptions, both confirmed by a prototype on a scratch copy: ...'. Each is a self-contained claim with no step numbers or teaser. Weakness: the headline and para-2 leads run 31-32 words (lint long-lead), so they are dense, but they are not shorthand.

expectations.text: `git status --porcelain` in OUTPUT_DIR/repo is empty: no code or doc was changed.
expectations.evidence: git -C outputs/repo status --porcelain printed nothing (exit 0); check_run repo_clean=true. Transcript step 8 shows experiments ran on a scratch copy (cp -R repo <scratchpad>/bp-overdue/repo).

notes: The plan is substantively strong: every cited file:line I spot-checked resolves, the prototype genuinely validated the clock plumbing and the closed-ticket edge, and the spec table is accurate. Both failures are prose discipline (a four-sentence headline, 91 lint findings dominated by semicolons), which is exactly what the old skill does not enforce, so the assertions discriminate well. Two eval notes: (1) check_run.py's section-order heuristic matches 'plan' against the H1 title and reports sections_in_order=false on a correctly ordered file; it should restrict matching to '## ' headings or skip the title line. (2) The headline assertion bundles a hard count (1-3 sentences) with a content check; a plan can state what-and-approach perfectly and still fail on count, which is intended but worth knowing when reading pass rates. No assertion checks that experiments ran outside OUTPUT_DIR/repo other than via git status, which a run that reverted its edits would also pass; the transcript's command list is the only evidence and nothing grades it.
